chapter: Ellington, singers, the book and closing
title: If he could redo things: pushing the atomic button for a fresh start
summary: Mingus says he would blow up a few places so people could start over with more love.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Yeah. Last question: If there was anything -- if you had the power to redo anything, is there anything you've done that you wouldn't do, or anything that you didn't do that you wish you had?
Yeah, man. I wish I could find -- see, I'm going to say this, --
Yeah.

And it may shock you. I mean, but I have a feeling that life didn't get started by no accident. That when the atomic bomb blew up Hiroshima and all that, I wish I knew the guy that knew where the button was. I would push it for freedom. Because I have the feeling that --
(Unintelligible.)
No, that's what I'm trying to explain.
Now, as I understood it, you would push the button for freedom --
Now, hold it. This is not a new idea. I've had this in my mind for a long time.
Yeah.
Now, they said the world would be destroyed, (inaudible) just cut it down to a few people.
Yeah.

I never seen such a mess. If they start over again, they might start with a little love. Because, man, the whole it looks in the Middle East and all this bullshit that's going on, look like it's going to be a big blowup everywhere. But I would just blow up a few places.
So what you're really -- you're fundamentally an optimist about people, because you think if you can sort of reduce it back to the beginning again, it would work out better.
I do.
Why would it work out better?
Well, might be a couple of men and women left.
Yeah.
Like Adam and Eve.
What kind of music do you think would come out of that new beginning?
Well, it's too bad you can't have one of those places like the President has got, where everybody
goes down in the ground, and have Charlie Parker down there, and Einstein, --
Yeah.
And a good person from every -- a Noah's Ark, underground.
Right, right, right.
That's what I mean.
Yeah. Is there anything I haven't asked about -
Everybody's going to die, anyway. That's my point.
